paragraphs: This paper asks whether an image classifier can improve after training without updating its learned parameters. Its central observation is that layers near the output retain useful information about image classes that the final output does not contain. A model's existing internal representations therefore offer another source of evidence for making predictions.

The proposed addition is a simple key-value cache that uses extracted network features as keys. It brings this extra information into classification at test time without training or fine-tuning the cache component. The approach can attach to a pretrained model, with two hyperparameters controlling its use. This makes the contribution a way to reuse an existing model's representations.

Experiments report classification improvements across multiple architectures and datasets. Features near the output work best as cache keys, and combining features from several layers can improve on using one layer alone. The authors also report a regularizing effect and substantially increased resistance to adversarial attacks. These findings describe observed improvements, rather than a guarantee of protection against every attack.
neurips-2018-a-simple-cache-model-for-im.tldr: A training-free cache uses information from a pretrained image classifier's internal layers to improve classification and observed adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: This paper constructs Gaussian process priors for several related outputs whose behavior must satisfy linear differential equations. The goal is to combine uncertain, noisy measurements with mathematical relationships that are specified precisely. Instead of treating those equations as information separate from the probabilistic model, the construction incorporates them into the prior itself.

The method uses Gröbner bases, an algebraic computational tool, to attempt to describe all solutions through a parameterization. If that attempt succeeds, a Gaussian process is passed through the parameterization to obtain the desired constrained prior. The conditional nature of this step matters: the abstract does not claim that the required parameterization can always be found.

The authors consider examples from physics, geomathematics, and control, including the full inhomogeneous Maxwell equations. These examples illustrate the intended connection between symbolic computation and statistical learning. The contribution is an algorithmic route from equations to probabilistic models, allowing exact algebraic structure and noisy observations to participate in the same modeling framework.
neurips-2018-algorithmic-linearly-constr.tldr: An algebraic construction produces Gaussian process priors satisfying linear differential equations when a suitable solution parameterization can be found.

paragraphs: ChannelNets address the difficulty of using large convolutional neural networks in applications with limited resources. The paper targets connections among feature maps, replacing dense connectivity with sparse connectivity through channel-wise convolutions. The intended benefit is to reduce both stored parameters and computation while retaining useful recognition capability.

The resulting architectures use three forms of this operation: group channel-wise convolutions, depth-wise separable channel-wise convolutions, and a convolutional classification layer. The final component extends compression to the classification stage. The authors highlight this as their first attempt to compress a fully connected classification layer, a component they say typically holds about a quarter of the parameters in compact CNNs.

On ImageNet, the authors report consistently better performance than prior methods. They also report substantial parameter and computational reductions compared with earlier CNNs designed for mobile devices, without an accuracy loss. The findings support sparse connections across feature maps as a useful design choice for compact networks, including a classification stage that remains a substantial part of an already small model.
neurips-2018-channelnets-compact-and-eff.tldr: ChannelNets use sparse connections among feature maps to reduce CNN parameters and computation while preserving accuracy in the reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Pairwise measurements appear in tasks such as combining rankings, learning from relative comparisons, and crowdsourcing. A difficulty is that an algorithm may assume the wrong statistical model for those measurements. This paper studies a more flexible model that keeps a natural exponential-family structure while leaving its base measure unspecified.

That formulation contains familiar models, including Bradley-Terry-Luce and paired cardinal models, as special cases. To estimate it without choosing the unknown base measure, the authors augment the data with virtual examples. These examples make it possible to construct a contrastive estimator, giving the learning procedure a way to operate despite the unspecified part of the measurement distribution.

The authors prove that the estimator is invariant to model misspecification within the stated natural exponential family. This qualification defines the scope of the robustness result. They also establish a statistical convergence rate that is optimal up to a logarithmic factor. Numerical experiments support the theory, connecting the flexible modeling choice to both robustness and efficient use of observations.
neurips-2018-contrastive-learning-from-p.tldr: Virtual comparison examples enable a contrastive estimator with robustness to misspecification within a natural exponential family and nearly optimal statistical convergence.

paragraphs: Variational inference learns graphical models by approximating their posterior distributions with a more manageable family of distributions. Choosing that family creates a central tension: it must be expressive enough to approximate the posterior while remaining computationally useful. This paper proposes coupled variational Bayes as a way to address that choice.

The approach generates the approximation family through an optimization procedure, which the authors call optimization embedding. It uses a primal-dual view of the evidence lower bound, or ELBO, to connect this construction to model learning. The approximate distribution is coupled to the graphical model's parameters, allowing training to backpropagate through the distribution-generating procedure and update the model end to end.

The theoretical analysis connects the method to gradient flow and establishes strong flexibility of the implicit distribution family in a limiting sense. That is a statement about the limit, rather than a promise of exact finite computation. Experiments on graphical models with continuous or discrete latent variables demonstrate effectiveness in comparisons with state-of-the-art methods.
neurips-2018-coupled-variational-bayes-v.tldr: Coupled variational Bayes generates posterior approximations through optimization, linking their flexibility and training directly to graphical-model parameters.

paragraphs: MubyNet estimates the locations, three-dimensional poses, and body shapes of multiple people from a single image. It works from detected body parts upward, rather than requiring the number of people or their visibility relationships in advance. A central challenge is combining discrete decisions about which parts belong together with continuous predictions of three-dimensional structure.

The network identifies joints and limbs, then scores possible groupings using learned combinations of two-dimensional and three-dimensional information. An integer-program formulation assembles partial or complete skeleton hypotheses subject to constraints from the body's kinematic tree. Joint reasoning avoids the suboptimality the authors associate with separating grouping in the image from reasoning about three-dimensional pose.

A final learned attention process integrates information from different body parts to predict pose and shape. The paper reports state-of-the-art results on Human3.6M and Panoptic, alongside qualitative reconstructions of multiple people under occlusion in difficult images. These findings support treating grouping and three-dimensional estimation as connected parts of one system.
neurips-2018-deep-network-for-the-integr.tldr: MubyNet combines two-dimensional and three-dimensional body-part evidence to group people and estimate their poses and shapes from one image.

paragraphs: This paper studies information-theoretic quantities in a class of stochastic deep learning models. Entropy describes uncertainty, while mutual information describes how much information variables share. Having a tractable way to calculate these quantities allows the authors to examine how information changes across a network and during learning.

The main calculations use heuristic methods from statistical physics under the assumption that weight matrices are independent and orthogonally invariant. The paper separately strengthens the rigorous foundation of particular cases: using adaptive interpolation, it proves exactness for two-layer networks with Gaussian random weights. The distinction between the broader heuristic derivation and this narrower proof is central to interpreting the results.

The authors also build synthetic-data experiments and constrain network weights so the required assumption holds during training. Within this controlled setting, they track entropy and mutual information throughout learning. Their conclusion is deliberately unresolved: the relationship between compression and generalization remains elusive. The work supplies analytical tools and a test setting without establishing compression as a general explanation of generalization.
neurips-2018-entropy-and-mutual-informat.tldr: The paper develops information calculations for constrained stochastic networks but finds no clear compression–generalization relationship in its experimental setting.

paragraphs: Conditional density estimation predicts a distribution of possible outcomes for a given input. Its challenge is to represent varied distributions without making the model unnecessarily complex or prone to overfitting. This paper proposes a Gaussian process approach in which the observed input is expanded with latent variables.

The Gaussian process maps this augmented input to samples from the conditional distribution. Latent variables provide a way to represent variation among outcomes under the same observed condition. The Bayesian formulation supports modeling with small datasets, while stochastic variational inference provides machinery for applying the approach to large datasets as well.

The model can share learned structure between conditions and represent densities in regions with sparse observations. This matters when information available for one condition can help inform another. The authors illustrate the method on taxi drop-off distributions across space and time, non-Gaussian noise modeling, and few-shot learning with Omniglot images. These applications demonstrate the range of conditional-distribution problems addressed by the same modeling approach.
neurips-2018-gaussian-process-conditiona.tldr: A Gaussian process maps observed conditions and latent variables to distribution samples, supporting shared structure across conditions and inference at different data scales.

paragraphs: A model can potentially discriminate by relying on information that stands in for a protected demographic attribute. This paper gives a definition of that proxy use for linear regression and develops algorithms to detect it. The focus is on identifying model behavior that could help explain discriminatory predictions.

The definition requires two properties together: a constituent part of the model must closely correlate with the protected variable, and it must causally influence the model's overall behavior. Correlation alone therefore does not establish proxy use under this definition. The authors show that qualifying proxies can be efficiently identified through a second-order cone program, turning the definition into a computational detection method.

The method is extended to settings where a particular input's use is justified as a business necessity. Empirical work on two law-enforcement datasets examines models with different degrees of racial disparity in their predictions. The reported findings show that detected proxies can illuminate causes of discriminatory behavior, providing an explanation of model reliance alongside observations of unequal outcomes.
neurips-2018-hunting-for-discriminatory-.tldr: The paper defines and efficiently detects influential demographic proxies in linear regression, helping explain discriminatory prediction behavior.

paragraphs: A memory system must retrieve a stored pattern even when its input is noisy or other memories interfere. Attractor dynamics address this by repeatedly refining a pattern during recall. The difficulty for deep learning is that the regions drawing states toward a memory have vanishing gradients, which make neural-network training difficult.

This paper uses variational inference to train a generative distributed memory while avoiding that vanishing-gradient problem. Its construction uses a Lyapunov function based on a variational lower bound, connecting the training formulation to the memory's iterative dynamics. The aim is to make repeated cleanup compatible with learning a generative memory model.

The resulting model has comparatively few parameters. Experiments show iterative retrieval converging to the correct patterns, and the authors report competitive performance both as a memory model and as a generative model. These findings connect two roles in one system: recovering stored structure from a disturbed input and modeling patterns generatively. The reported convergence is an experimental finding about the tested retrieval behavior.
neurips-2018-learning-attractor-dynamics.tldr: A variationally trained generative memory incorporates attractor dynamics to clean up recalled patterns while avoiding the associated vanishing-gradient problem.

paragraphs: This paper approaches software-vulnerability repair as learning a transformation between discrete domains. The central question is whether a useful repair mapping can be learned without labeled examples pairing each source item with its desired target. Removing that requirement changes the kind of training data the method needs.

The proposed approach uses adversarial learning to learn the mapping. It also does not require a bijection between the source and target domains, meaning it does not impose an exact one-to-one correspondence. Together, these properties allow the formulation to address transformations where paired supervision and a one-to-one domain relationship are unavailable.

For software repair, the authors report performance close to sequence-to-sequence approaches that do require labeled pairs. The claim is competitive performance despite different supervision requirements, rather than superiority over those approaches. They also describe the method as application-agnostic and identify grammar correction and sentiment translation as possible uses. Those examples indicate the broader scope of the formulation; the stated demonstration concerns vulnerability repair.
neurips-2018-learning-to-repair-software.tldr: An adversarial approach learns software-vulnerability repairs without paired labels and performs close to sequence-to-sequence methods that require them.

paragraphs: This paper treats solving SMT formulas as a search over sequences of formula transformations. At each step, the system chooses a transformation and continues until the formula is solved. The learning problem is therefore to choose useful moves through this search, rather than to replace the solver's underlying reasoning machinery.

The approach has two stages. First, it learns a policy from a collection of unsolved formulas that selects transformations during solving. It then converts the policy's decisions into a program with branches and no loops. This program provides an interpretable strategy that can guide an existing SMT solver without changing the solver itself or evaluating the learned policy during inference.

Across the reported benchmarks, the approach solves 17% more formulas and delivers runtime improvements of up to 100 times over a state-of-the-art solver. The largest speedup is a reported maximum, not a uniform gain. The practical contribution is the conversion of learned search decisions into a directly usable solver strategy.
neurips-2018-learning-to-solve-smt-formu.tldr: A learned transformation policy is compiled into an interpretable program that improves SMT solving without modifying the solver or running the policy at inference.

paragraphs: MetaAnchor changes how anchor-based object detectors use prior boxes. Many detectors define their anchor mechanisms in advance, tying detection behavior to those choices. This paper instead proposes generating anchor functions dynamically from customized prior boxes, making the anchor mechanism more flexible.

The approach uses weight prediction to generate the functions associated with the requested boxes. In this way, a box specification becomes an input to the construction of the detection function. The authors state that the mechanism can work with most anchor-based detection systems, including RetinaNet, so its role is to modify an existing detector's handling of anchors.

Experiments on COCO show consistent improvements over the compared counterparts across the tested scenarios. The authors also find greater robustness to anchor settings and bounding-box distributions. These results support the value of adapting anchor functions rather than relying on a predefined scheme. The abstract additionally reports potential for transfer tasks, which is a more tentative claim than the observed detection improvements.
neurips-2018-metaanchor-learning-to-dete.tldr: MetaAnchor predicts anchor functions from customized prior boxes, improving detection and robustness to anchor choices in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper learns causal relationships in linear systems using observational data from multiple domains. Across those domains, causal coefficients, exogenous-noise distributions, or both may change. The method treats these changes as information for identifying causal direction, rather than requiring all domains to exhibit the same relationships.

Its central principle is that, in a causally sufficient system, causal modules and their parameters change independently across domains. The authors first develop efficient methods for determining direction between two variables, then extend the approach to networks of variables. The assumptions about linear systems and independent changes define the setting in which this reasoning is applied.

Earlier approaches often depend on some causal modules remaining invariant across domains. This work incorporates that idea but also handles cases without such invariance. The authors state that their methods generally identify direction with fewer than ten domains, and that two domains are generally sufficient when invariance holds. These are qualified sufficiency claims, not universal minimum requirements for every system.
neurips-2018-multi-domain-causal-structu.tldr: Independent changes across domains help identify causal structure in linear systems, including settings without invariant causal modules.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations describe hidden-state evolution continuously. A neural network specifies the state's derivative, and a differential-equation solver computes the resulting output. This replaces a prescribed sequence of hidden layers with a learned rule for how the state changes.

The paper presents models with constant memory cost, input-dependent evaluation strategies, and an explicit tradeoff between numerical precision and speed. These properties are demonstrated in continuous-depth residual networks and continuous-time latent-variable models. The solver's role matters because computing the model output becomes a numerical integration problem whose precision can be controlled.

The authors also construct continuous normalizing flows that support maximum-likelihood training without partitioning or ordering data dimensions. To make the broader framework trainable, they show how to backpropagate scalably through an ODE solver without accessing its internal operations. This allows a differential-equation component to participate in end-to-end learning inside a larger model, connecting continuous dynamics with ordinary neural-network training workflows.
neurips-2018-neural-ordinary-differentia.tldr: Neural ODEs learn continuous hidden-state dynamics and train through differential-equation solvers, enabling adaptive evaluation and continuous generative models.

paragraphs: Many learning systems convert a vector of scores into probabilities, whether for classification or attention. This paper studies the relationship among several such mappings, including softmax, sum-normalization, spherical softmax, and sparsemax. It focuses particularly on controlling sparsity: how many entries receive zero probability.

The authors develop a common framework containing these existing mappings as special cases. It provides simple closed-form solutions and subgradients suitable for backpropagation. Within it, they introduce sparsegen-lin and sparsehourglass, two formulations intended to offer control over the desired degree of sparsity. This makes sparsity a property the mapping is designed to regulate.

The paper also develops convex losses to encourage the proposed mappings' behavior in multilabel classification, where experiments show improved performance. When used for attention in machine translation and abstractive summarization, the formulations achieve better or comparable results on the reported tasks. The findings support controllable sparse mappings as useful alternatives, without claiming that greater sparsity always improves a model.
neurips-2018-on-controllable-sparse-alte.tldr: A unified framework connects probability mappings and introduces sparse alternatives with explicit control over sparsity and competitive empirical performance.

paragraphs: This paper studies model compression through knowledge transfer, where a stronger teacher network helps train a smaller student. The motivation is to make deep networks usable in embedded systems while limiting performance degradation. Its proposed transfer method changes how the teacher's knowledge is represented for the student.

Two convolutional modules perform the transfer. A paraphraser is trained without supervision to extract teacher factors, which are transformed representations of information in the teacher network. A translator in the student extracts student factors and learns by mimicking the teacher factors. The transfer target is therefore an intermediate representation produced specifically for this exchange.

The authors report that students trained through this factor-transfer method outperform students trained with conventional knowledge-transfer methods in their experiments. This supports the idea that the form of the transferred information matters, alongside the teacher's strength. The contribution is a concrete way to prepare teacher representations and align student representations with them, so a compact network can benefit from a stronger one during training.
neurips-2018-paraphrasing-complex-networ.tldr: Factor transfer trains a compact student to mimic transformed teacher representations using convolutional paraphraser and translator modules.

paragraphs: Policy optimization for continuous control can alternate between collecting trajectories and improving a policy using the collected data. Reusing trajectories can make learning more efficient, but it raises a decision: when should offline improvement stop and new experience be gathered? The paper identifies uncertainty in the estimated objective as central to that decision.

The proposed model-free algorithm, POIS, begins with a high-confidence bound for importance-sampling estimation. The authors then use this foundation to define a surrogate objective that is optimized offline after each new batch of trajectories arrives. This connects policy improvement on reused data with an explicit treatment of the estimate's uncertainty.

POIS applies in both action-based and parameter-based settings. The authors test it on a selection of continuous-control tasks using linear and deep policies, with comparisons to state-of-the-art optimization methods. The abstract describes this evaluation without stating a performance ranking. Its main stated contribution is an uncertainty-aware foundation for policy search that repeatedly optimizes over collected experience.
neurips-2018-policy-optimization-via-imp.tldr: POIS uses a high-confidence importance-sampling bound to build an offline policy-optimization objective for reusing collected trajectories.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to improve randomized feature maps used to approximate kernels. Such maps help scale kernel methods to larger datasets. The starting point is that these approximations arise by applying Monte Carlo estimation to integral representations of kernel functions.

The authors approach the problem through numerical integration. They propose a unifying method based on an efficient integration technique that both reinterprets earlier random-feature approaches and extends them toward better kernel estimates. This perspective links feature construction to the problem of approximating an integral: improving the integration procedure provides a route to improving the resulting kernel approximation.

The paper derives the method's convergence behavior and reports an extensive empirical study supporting its hypothesis. The theoretical analysis addresses how the approximation converges, while the experiments supply evidence for the proposed improvement. The stated contribution combines an explanation of existing random-feature methods with a way to extend them. Its focus is the quality of kernel approximation within the broader effort to make kernel methods practical for larger datasets.
neurips-2018-quadrature-based-features-f.tldr: A numerical-integration framework unifies earlier random-feature methods and develops improved kernel approximations supported by convergence analysis and experiments.

paragraphs: This paper studies sequential portfolio selection when each portfolio may contain at most k assets. The learner repeatedly allocates investments while aiming for strong long-term returns. The cardinality restriction makes the choice of which assets to include an explicit part of the learning problem.

The authors consider two information settings. Under full feedback, the learner observes return-to-cost ratios for every asset. Under bandit feedback, it observes those ratios only for assets it invested in. They give efficient algorithms with sublinear regret in both cases, meaning the regret bounds grow more slowly than the number of rounds.

Statistical lower bounds nearly match the upper bounds when k is constant, showing that the guarantees approach the limits identified by the analysis in that setting. A separate computational lower bound establishes a tension between efficiency and obtaining a small regret upper bound. Together, the results distinguish what limited observations make statistically difficult from what the portfolio-selection problem makes computationally difficult.
neurips-2018-regret-bounds-for-online-po.tldr: The paper gives sublinear-regret algorithms for portfolios with limited asset counts and establishes statistical and computational limits in two feedback settings.

paragraphs: Rendering turns a three-dimensional shape into a two-dimensional image. Working backward from an image is difficult when rendering includes discrete operations, such as deciding which surfaces are visible, that obstruct differentiation. This paper addresses that obstacle with a learned renderer designed to support gradients.

RenderNet is a convolutional network with a projection unit that converts three-dimensional shape information into an image. The network automatically encodes spatial occlusion and shading calculations. The authors position this approach against existing differentiable renderers whose handling of occlusion and range of rendering effects remain restricted.

Experiments show that RenderNet can learn different shaders and can support inverse rendering from a single image. The estimated properties include shape, pose, lighting, and texture. These findings demonstrate the usefulness of a learned rendering process for connecting image appearance to scene parameters. They establish that the network can perform the reported inverse tasks, rather than that every image uniquely determines the scene that produced it.
neurips-2018-rendernet-a-deep-convolutio.tldr: RenderNet learns differentiable rendering with occlusion and shading, enabling single-image estimation of shape, pose, lighting, and texture.

paragraphs: Navigation instructions usually describe landmarks and major decisions, leaving many movements unstated. An instruction-following system must fill those gaps using what it sees. This paper addresses both the shortage of annotated navigation data and the difficulty of learning that reasoning with generic sequence models.

The approach adds a speaker model with two jobs. It generates additional instructions for training, and it evaluates how well candidate action sequences explain a given instruction. The second use supplies pragmatic reasoning: possible routes are assessed through the language they would account for. A panoramic action space supports both uses by matching the level of detail in human instructions.

Experiments show that speaker-generated training data, pragmatic reasoning, and the panoramic action space each substantially improve the baseline follower. The complete approach more than doubles the success rate of the best existing method on the reported standard benchmark. The results support combining instruction generation with instruction following, so language modeling helps both expand training data and evaluate possible navigation behavior.
neurips-2018-speaker-follower-models-for.tldr: A speaker model supplies synthetic instructions and evaluates candidate routes, helping more than double navigation success on the reported benchmark.

paragraphs: Feedforward convolutional networks can classify objects and model time-averaged responses in the primate visual system. Biological vision also contains local recurrent connections and feedback from later areas to earlier ones. This paper investigates whether incorporating those architectural features improves recognition and better accounts for neural activity over time.

Simply inserting standard recurrence is insufficient in the reported experiments: vanilla recurrent networks and LSTMs perform poorly within deep CNNs on ImageNet. New recurrent cells with bypassing and gating substantially improve accuracy. The authors then search thousands of architectures using these design principles, identifying useful local recurrent cells and long-range feedback connections.

The resulting task-optimized convolutional recurrent networks match the dynamics of primate visual activity better than feedforward networks. This links success on object recognition to a closer match with changing neural responses, beyond time-averaged activity alone. The findings suggest that recurrent connections contribute to difficult visual behavior; they do not establish that the discovered architectures are exact descriptions of the brain.
neurips-2018-task-driven-convolutional-r.tldr: Carefully designed recurrence improves object recognition and matches primate visual-response dynamics better than feedforward networks in the reported study.

paragraphs: Training deep networks demands substantial computation, motivating arithmetic formats that pack more performance into accelerator hardware. Fixed-point arithmetic is attractive for hardware density, but its narrow dynamic range creates difficulties for training convergence. This paper investigates block floating point as a way to retain a wider range while using fixed-point logic for much of the computation.

Because block floating point alone has limitations that prevent direct use, the authors introduce a hybrid format called HBFP. It performs all dot products in block floating point and other operations in floating point. The design assigns different arithmetic representations to different kinds of computation, aiming to combine training accuracy with dense hardware implementation.

Across a wide variety of models, the authors report accuracy matching floating-point training. They also show that the approach enables hardware implementations with throughput improvements of up to 8.5 times. That figure is an upper reported improvement, not a uniform speedup across all models. The results support hybrid arithmetic as a practical design direction for training accelerators.
neurips-2018-training-dnns-with-hybrid-b.tldr: HBFP combines block-floating-point dot products with floating-point operations to match reported training accuracy while enabling up to 8.5 times higher hardware throughput.

paragraphs: This paper studies a simplified expanding economy in which producers repeatedly make goods, trade them, and use the goods they receive as inputs for the next production round. Each producer must decide how to distribute money among bids for available goods. Those repeated investment decisions connect individual behavior to the economy's long-term development.

The proposed decentralized rule updates bids in proportion to how useful earlier investments were. Producers therefore adjust their spending using the usefulness of their own purchases. The authors show that this simple dynamic leads to long-term economic growth whenever growth is possible within the model.

The same dynamic also produces unbounded inequality, with very rich and very poor participants emerging. Aggregate expansion therefore coexists with increasingly unequal outcomes in this setting. The paper further analyzes how a participant's relationships with others affect its development and examines the system's Gini index. These results describe the modeled production economy and its update rule, connecting a growth guarantee to a sharply unequal distribution of its benefits.
neurips-2018-universal-growth-in-product.tldr: In a simplified production economy, proportional bid updates achieve growth whenever possible while also generating unbounded inequality.
